name: CagriSema
route: Once-weekly injection under the skin in trials
status: Not FDA-approved as of this writing. Submitted in December 2025 for weight management; decision anticipated by late 2026
mechanism: Combines semaglutide (a GLP-1 drug) and cagrilintide (an amylin analog) in one weekly injection to lower appetite through two pathways

article.summary: CagriSema is a once-weekly injection combining semaglutide and the amylin analog cagrilintide. Phase 3 trials showed about 20% weight loss, and Novo Nordisk has asked the FDA to approve it for weight management.
article.takeaway: CagriSema is a once-weekly injection that combines [semaglutide](/peptides/semaglutide), the GLP-1 drug in Ozempic and Wegovy, with [cagrilintide](/peptides/cagrilintide), an amylin analog. In the 68-week REDEFINE 1 trial of 3,417 adults with obesity, average weight fell by **20.4%** versus 3.0% on placebo, and in adults who also had type 2 diabetes the figures were 13.7% versus 3.4%.[^1][^2] In a head-to-head trial it did not match tirzepatide (20.2% versus 23.6% at 84 weeks).[^3] Novo Nordisk asked the FDA to approve it in December 2025 and anticipated a decision by late 2026.[^3]
glance: Submitted to the FDA for weight management in December 2025; decision anticipated by late 2026
Once-weekly injection under the skin (in trials)
Phase 3 REDEFINE (obesity) and REIMAGINE (type 2 diabetes) programs

blocks.text: CagriSema pairs two hormone copies in one pen. Semaglutide mimics GLP-1, which raises insulin when blood sugar is high, slows stomach emptying and quiets hunger signals. Cagrilintide mimics amylin, a hormone released with insulin that promotes fullness through partly separate brain pathways. The aim is more weight loss than either ingredient gives alone. In REDEFINE 1, more people reached a BMI under 27 and a waist-to-height ratio under 0.53 on CagriSema (30.3%) than on semaglutide (19.1%) or cagrilintide (9.0%) alone.[^4]

Novo Nordisk submitted CagriSema to the FDA in December 2025 for weight management in adults with obesity, based on REDEFINE 1 and REDEFINE 2, and said a decision was anticipated by late 2026.[^3] A cardiovascular outcomes trial (REDEFINE 3) and a type 2 diabetes program (REIMAGINE) are also under way or reported.[^5][^6] A higher-dose CagriSema trial was planned to start in the second half of 2026.[^3]

rows: 1,206 adults with obesity and type 2 diabetes

HbA1c fell 1.91 points vs 1.75 on semaglutide alone[^6]

blocks.text: REDEFINE 4 compared CagriSema directly with tirzepatide and did not meet its goal of showing equivalent weight loss.[^3]

items: **Digestive effects** were most common: nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, constipation or abdominal pain affected 79.6% on CagriSema versus 39.9% on placebo in REDEFINE 1, mostly transient and mild to moderate.[^1]
**In type 2 diabetes** (REDEFINE 2), 72.5% versus 34.4% had digestive events.[^2]
**Class pattern:** the safety profile in REIMAGINE 2 was described as consistent with GLP-1 drugs and earlier cagrilintide data.[^6]
**Unknown:** long-term safety, and whether CagriSema lowers heart attacks and strokes, will depend on the ongoing outcomes trial.[^5]

blocks.text: No approved CagriSema product exists. FDA says cagrilintide cannot be used in compounding under federal law, so any product sold as CagriSema before approval is unapproved and its contents are unverified.[^7]

The FDA decision on weight management is the next milestone, followed by REDEFINE 11 data (expected in the first half of 2027) and a planned higher-dose trial, both designed to test how much weight loss the combination can reach.[^3]

evidence.label: Strong for weight loss; trails tirzepatide head to head
evidence.text: Large randomized phase 3 trials in people with and without type 2 diabetes show clear weight loss and better blood sugar control than semaglutide alone.[^1][^2][^6] The head-to-head result against tirzepatide and the lack of heart outcome data are the main gaps.[^3][^5]

faq.a: Not as of this writing. Novo Nordisk submitted it to the FDA in December 2025 and anticipated a decision by late 2026.[^3]

faq.q: Does CagriSema work better than semaglutide alone?
faq.a: In REIMAGINE 2 it lowered HbA1c slightly more (1.91 vs 1.75 points),[^6] and in REDEFINE 1 more people reached healthier BMI and waist targets (30.3% vs 19.1%).[^4]

faq.q: How does it compare with tirzepatide?
faq.a: In the open-label REDEFINE 4 trial, CagriSema produced less weight loss than tirzepatide 15 mg (20.2% vs 23.6% at 84 weeks) and did not meet non-inferiority.[^3]
Not legally for human use. Because FDA says cagrilintide cannot be compounded, online products sold as CagriSema are unapproved and of unknown quality.[^7]
